about:
![Hourstone: blue rune stone with a golden hourglass](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/main/docs/assets/Logo.png)

# Hourstone – Azeroth Playtime Tracker

**Your characters. Your time.**

Track your World of Warcraft characters and their total `/played` time in one compact window. In Retail, switch to **Progress** to check keystones, your weekly Mythic+ best and Great Vault slots across your characters. Search by character or guild, filter realms and client families, and size the window up to 200%. German and English interfaces are included.

[Download](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/releases/latest) · [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/hourstone-azeroth-hours) · [Deutsche Anleitung](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/DEUTSCH.md) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/issues)

![Hourstone playtime overview with characters, guilds and realm and client filters](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/main/docs/assets/addon-overview-en.png)

The character overview puts realm and client filters beside the search and shows each character's guild and playtime. Images show the implemented interface rendered with example characters.

## Installation

1. Download the `Hourstone-X.Y.Z.zip` asset from GitHub Releases or install through CurseForge.
2. Exit WoW and extract the ZIP into the client's `Interface/AddOns` directory.
3. Confirm the result is `Interface/AddOns/Hourstone/Hourstone.toc`, enable Hourstone and log in.

Repeat for each installation. The addon runs independently without another addon or an external account. GitHub's source archives are intended for development.

## Features and controls

- Character name, class, level, realm and guild, with a separate client column beside playtime and last update.
- Search by character or guild, realm and client filters together above the table, sortable columns, total and filtered playtime.
- Decimal hours or days / hours / minutes, plus the current login session.
- Delete entries from the overview without losing their saved playtime; restore them from a separate list.
- Retail **Time played / Progress** tabs with the current keystone, highest completed Mythic+ level this week and nine Great Vault slots.
- Entry in WoW's **Addons menu** below the clock where the client provides it: left click opens or closes Hourstone. On those clients the draggable minimap button is off by default after the update and can be turned back on in the settings or with `/hourstone minimap`.
- Movable window, 65–200% size setting in 5% steps and optional draggable minimap button. Larger scales show fewer rows and scroll; the window only shrinks when its width or minimum height cannot fit.
- `/hourstone` or `/azerothhours`: open or close; `/hourstone minimap`: show or hide the minimap button; `/hourstone reset`: reset window position.

Use the gear button for display settings and drag the title bar to move the window. Version 0.3.1 fixes the window jumping back during a drag; its position is saved when you release it. Click column headings to sort, including client names, scroll longer lists, and hover a character for full details. Unknown client families sort last. Tooltips show the recorded data and the last server timestamp without claiming an online/offline status.

## Retail progress

![Hourstone Retail progress with keystones, weekly Mythic+ best and Great Vault slots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/main/docs/assets/addon-progress-en.png)

The **Progress** tab keeps the character, realm and guild beside the current keystone, the highest completed Mythic+ level this week, and three slots each for Dungeon, Raid and World activities. Hover a progress cell or Vault row for details and its capture time. The gear menu controls size up to 200%; search and realm/client filters work in both views. Classic clients keep the playtime view.

Hourstone reads the logged-in character's keystone, localized dungeon name, completed weekly runs and Vault thresholds from Blizzard's APIs. Completed overtime runs count toward the weekly best; abandoned runs do not. Dungeon abbreviations and seasonal thresholds are not hard-coded. A dungeon name may be shortened to fit, but its key level stays visible and the tooltip contains the full name.

Each character must be visited with this version before its progress can be recorded. Offline characters show the last captured data. **No keystone**, **Not yet recorded** and **Outdated** are distinct states; a weekly reset makes old progress stale until a new observation. Previous rewards are not presented as this week's progress, and temporary or protected API values do not erase valid data.

WoW saves locally recorded progress at logout or `/reload`. Companion versions supporting [protocol 4](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/sync-protocol-v4.md) can synchronize it between selected installations and accounts. Received progress is displayed alongside local observations without becoming a local measurement. Older Companions continue to synchronize playtime, guilds and delete/restore controls.

## Deleting and restoring overview entries

Right-click a character and confirm **Delete** to hide it from the overview and its totals. This never deletes a WoW character or its saved playtime. In the gear menu, choose **Deleted characters**, then right-click an entry to restore it. Use the same menu to return to tracked characters. The summary cards always exclude deleted entries, including while browsing that list.

A new login with that character also restores deletions already known to the addon. Deleting your currently played character's entry keeps it hidden until you restore it or log in again; its time continues to be recorded. `/reload`, zoning and `/played` do not restore it. If another PC deleted the entry while this PC was offline, synchronize first and then make a new character login. These changes are saved with the normal WoW logout/reload and exchanged by Companion.

## Tracking and saved data

A character appears after its first login with Hourstone enabled. The server's `/played` total includes time played before installation. Unvisited characters cannot be discovered automatically. Between server responses, only the active character's displayed time advances locally. Requests are separated by at least 60 seconds. AFK time counts; offline time does not.

The session continues through a UI reload identified by WoW and resets at a new login. Data is saved as `HourstoneDB` per installation and WoW account at logout or reload. A crash can lose unsaved changes.

Guild membership is recorded for each character when you play it. Guild changes and leaving a guild update independently of playtime. Characters without a recorded guild status show **Not yet recorded**; log in with Hourstone 0.2.1 or later and log out or `/reload` to make the guild available to the companion. **No guild** means the character was confirmed to be guildless. The last saved status is shown for offline characters.

## Optional synchronization

**Progress synchronization requires Companion 0.2.0 or newer on every participating PC.**
Use Companion 0.2.1 or newer with WoW 12.1.5 and WoW: Forever. Its data addon
Hourstone_Sync declares their interfaces, so WoW no longer lists it as out of date.
After updating the Companion, fully close and restart WoW once. Companion versions
before 0.2.0 remain compatible with their playtime, guild and visibility features.

Hourstone 0.3.2 supports [protocol 4](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/sync-protocol-v4.md) with a compatible [Hourstone Companion](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-companion), including Retail progress, guild membership and shared delete/restore controls. Companion 0.1.3–0.1.6 remains compatible for the existing protocol-3 features. Upgrading from the public 0.1.1 release migrates saved data to schema 3 while preserving existing characters and settings. An upgrade from 0.2.2 or later keeps SavedVariables schema 3 without another migration. Legacy protocol 1–3 input remains readable; Hourstone 0.1.x does not support the Companion. New Companions read the local progress cache from 0.3.1, but send progress back only to an addon advertising protocol-4 support.

WoW first saves by logging out or using `/reload`. The Companion reads the saved observations from your selected installations and accounts, combines them and makes the shared overview available to the addon. Hourstone reads that overview on the next login or `/reload`. After the initial installation of the Companion data addon, fully close and restart WoW once. Between PCs, choose a folder that Dropbox, OneDrive or another service synchronizes and keeps available locally on each device; the Companion exchanges device snapshots through that folder.

[Hourstone Companion 0.2.1 for Windows 11 x64](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-companion/releases/tag/v0.2.1) is available as an installer or portable package. This is an unsigned preview release; installations from GitHub update automatically. A Microsoft Store version is submitted separately and requires certification. Its repository contains setup information and source code. Hourstone remains fully usable on its own.

Repeated observations of the same character are merged, never added. Confirmed server measurements are stored separately from local estimates. UI settings, request timing and the current session remain local. Synchronization cannot transfer `/played` between distinct characters, fetch unvisited characters or update a running client in real time. The companion's documentation explains setup, backups and limitations.

## Supported clients

| Client family | Declared interface |
| --- | ---: |
| Retail | 120105 |
| Mists of Pandaria Classic | 50504 |
| Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary | 20506 |
| Classic Era | 11509 |
| WoW: Forever | 16001 |

WoW: Forever uses the Retail API and Hourstone's playtime view; keystones and the Great Vault do not exist there. There Hourstone wears Forever's own window frame, as Soundstone does: the bronze frame with its title strip, red gear and close buttons, Forever's dropdowns, red buttons and slider, and the character table on Blizzard's inset over the darkened rock. Where the client lacks a piece of that art, the piece falls back to a flat near-black look with a one-pixel bronze line. The look changes only the interface: class colors and the current character's marker stay as they are. Retail and the Classic clients keep their designs. In the Forever client, Hourstone shows its characters as **WoW: Forever** in the client column, tooltip and sorting, and the client filter offers WoW: Forever next to Retail. They remain in the Retail client family for saved keys and Companion protocol 4, which has no separate Forever family; Companion 0.2.1 and newer also label them as WoW: Forever. Since Hourstone 0.3.7, synchronized Forever characters that this account has not recorded itself, such as those of another account or PC, show as WoW: Forever on every client, Forever included, and the client filter offers WoW: Forever wherever such a character is listed. This needs Companion 0.2.2 or newer on the PC running WoW, which names the Forever installations in the data addon ([protocol 4 addendum](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/sync-protocol-v4-forever.md)); with an older Companion they stay under Retail. For characters it has recorded itself, an account's own label decides. On its first load in Forever, Hourstone 0.3.6 also labels the characters of a database it created there after the launch on 2026-11-04 at 23:00 UTC; in an older database, such as a `WTF` folder copied from Retail, characters switch to WoW: Forever at their next login in Forever. Forever characters have a surname, which the live client reports where other clients report the realm; since 0.3.7, Hourstone saves it as part of the name, such as "Magni Wildschuss", together with the realm WoW reports, such as "CAMWOW EU4 Realm 10 RP", and corrects each character at its next login. Hourstone never saves an empty realm or name. Hourstone has been tested in the live Forever client (build 1.60.1.70790). Beta characters do not carry over to the live game; if you copied the beta's `WTF` folder into `_forever_`, close WoW and move `Hourstone.lua` out of `_forever_\WTF\Account\*\SavedVariables` before your first live login, otherwise the beta characters stay in the list. Hardcore and Season of Discovery use the Era interface. See [validation](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/VALIDATION.md) for current in-game coverage and automated checks.

## Development

Use Python 3.12:

```sh
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python tools/install_hooks.py
python tools/privacy_guard.py
python tests/run.py
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
python tools/package.py
```

The local pre-push hook and CI check the current tree and every new commit for private material. Keep local exports, logs and credentials outside Git. [Repository checks](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/REPOSITORY.md) explains the historical baseline and checks.

`tools/assets.py` regenerates shipping TGA textures from retained PNG masters and source manifests. Packaging validates metadata, files, textures, licenses and deterministic ZIP output. `tools/preview.py` renders the current Lua layout with synthetic data and approximate browser fonts; native checks remain necessary. Add `--product-pages` to generate German and English product layouts for documentation images in `dist`.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), [validation guide](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/VALIDATION.md) and [publishing guide](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/curseforge/README.md).

## License and artwork

[MIT](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/LICENSE), © 2026 krebs3r. Hourstone shares its visual style with [Soundstone – Azeroth Audio](https://github.com/krebs3r/soundstone-azeroth-audio). Soundstone artwork retains its MIT license, and bundled fonts retain their SIL Open Font Licenses. See [artwork](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/ARTWORK.md) and [font provenance](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/main/docs/FONTS.md). World of Warcraft is a trademark of Blizzard Entertainment; Hourstone is an independent community addon.

releases.notes:
# Hourstone 0.4.2 — 2026-11-19

Hourstone has a new name that says what it does: **Hourstone – Azeroth Playtime
Tracker**. WoW's addon list, the window title, WoW: Forever's title strip and the
tooltips of the minimap button and the Addons menu show it. The addon folder, your
saved characters and settings, `/hourstone` and `/azerothhours` stay as they are;
nothing is migrated.

Everything else is as in
[Hourstone 0.4.1](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/releases/tag/v0.4.1).
With WoW closed, extract `Hourstone-0.4.2.zip` into `Interface/AddOns`.

Automated checks and the in-game test are described in
[validation](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/v0.4.2/docs/VALIDATION.md).

## Deutsch

Hourstone hat einen neuen Namen, der sagt, was es tut: **Hourstone – Azeroth Playtime
Tracker**. Die Addon-Liste von WoW, der Fenstertitel, die Titelleiste in WoW: Forever
und die Tooltips von Minimap-Button und Addons-Menü zeigen ihn. Addon-Ordner,
gespeicherte Charaktere und Einstellungen, `/hourstone` und `/azerothhours` bleiben
unverändert; es wird nichts migriert.

Alles andere ist wie in Hourstone 0.4.1. Das ZIP bei geschlossenem WoW nach
`Interface/AddOns` entpacken.

Die automatischen Prüfungen und der Test im Spiel stehen in der verlinkten Validierung.

releases.name: Hourstone 0.4.1 – Azeroth Hours
releases.notes:
# Hourstone 0.4.1 — 2026-11-10

Hourstone 0.4.1 shows Death Knights, Monks and Demon Hunters in their class colors
on clients whose own class table lacks these classes. In WoW: Forever this concerns
characters synchronized from Retail. Hourstone takes Blizzard's own colors for these
classes from the Classic clients' class color table; the client's own colors still
come first.

Everything else is as in [Hourstone 0.4.0](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/releases/tag/v0.4.0),
which gave the window WoW: Forever's own look in the Forever client: the bronze
window frame with its title strip, Forever's dropdowns, buttons and slider, and the
character table on the window's darkened rock. Retail, Mists Classic, TBC
Anniversary and Classic Era look as in 0.3.7. With WoW closed, extract
`Hourstone-0.4.1.zip` into `Interface/AddOns`.

Automated checks are described in [validation](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/v0.4.1/docs/VALIDATION.md).

## Deutsch

Hourstone 0.4.1 zeigt Todesritter, Mönche und Dämonenjäger in ihren Klassenfarben,
auch auf Clients, deren eigene Klassentabelle diese Klassen nicht kennt. In WoW:
Forever betrifft das von Retail synchronisierte Charaktere. Hourstone nimmt dafür
Blizzards eigene Farben aus der Klassenfarben-Tabelle der Classic-Clients; die Farben
des Clients haben weiter Vorrang.

Alles andere ist wie in Hourstone 0.4.0, das dem Fenster im Client von WoW: Forever
dessen eigenes Aussehen gegeben hat: den bronzenen Fensterrahmen mit Titelleiste,
Forevers Dropdowns, Knöpfe und Regler und die Charaktertabelle auf dem abgedunkelten
Fels des Fensters. Retail, Mists Classic, TBC Anniversary und Classic Era sehen aus
wie in 0.3.7. Das ZIP bei geschlossenem WoW nach `Interface/AddOns` entpacken.

Die automatischen Prüfungen stehen in der verlinkten Validierung.

releases.name: Hourstone 0.4.0 – Azeroth Hours
releases.notes:
# Hourstone 0.4.0 — 2026-11-10

Hourstone 0.4.0 gives the window **WoW: Forever's own look** in the Forever client,
as Soundstone 0.4.0 does. The window, the settings and the delete dialog wear the
client's bronze window frame with its rock ground and title strip; the gear and the
close button sit in the strip as red buttons, and the title takes the client's gold.
The search field, the realm and client filters and the Combined/Hours toggle share
Forever's dropdown field, and the menus open in Forever's dropdown list. Reset
position, Done, Deleted characters, Cancel and Delete are Blizzard's red buttons, and
the size slider has Forever's track and copper diamond. The character table lies in
Blizzard's inset frame on the window's rock, darkened so that class colors stay
legible. Inside the frame the window is 20 units shorter; a saved position keeps its
top edge.

Where the client lacks a piece of this art, that piece alone falls back to a flat
near-black look with a one-pixel bronze line. The look follows the client and has no
switch. Class colors and the current character's marker are unchanged. Retail, Mists
Classic, TBC Anniversary and Classic Era look exactly as in 0.3.7. Playtime, saved
keys, SavedVariables schema 3 and Companion protocol 4 are unchanged. With WoW
closed, extract `Hourstone-0.4.0.zip` into `Interface/AddOns`.

Automated checks are described in [validation](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/v0.4.0/docs/VALIDATION.md), the design in the [theme document](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/v0.4.0/docs/FOREVER-THEME.md).
The author tested the new look in the live Forever client. For Retail and the Classic
clients, an automated test compares every visible region with 0.3.7.

## Deutsch

Hourstone 0.4.0 gibt dem Fenster im Client von **WoW: Forever dessen eigenes
Aussehen**, wie Soundstone 0.4.0. Fenster, Einstellungen und Löschdialog tragen den
bronzenen Fensterrahmen des Clients mit Felsgrund und Titelleiste; Zahnrad und
Schließen-Knopf sitzen als rote Knöpfe in der Leiste, und der Titel erscheint im Gold
des Clients. Suchfeld, Realm- und Clientfilter und der Umschalter Tage + Std. /
Stunden teilen sich Forevers Dropdown-Feld, und die Menüs öffnen sich in Forevers
Dropdown-Liste. Position zurücksetzen, Fertig, Gelöschte Charaktere, Abbrechen und
Löschen sind Blizzards rote Knöpfe, und der Größenregler hat Forevers Schiene und
kupferne Raute. Die Charaktertabelle liegt in Blizzards Inset-Rahmen auf dem Fels des
Fensters, abgedunkelt, damit Klassenfarben gut lesbar bleiben. Im Rahmen ist das
Fenster 20 Einheiten niedriger; eine gespeicherte Position behält ihre Oberkante.

Fehlt dem Client ein Teil dieser Grafik, fällt nur dieser Teil auf ein flaches, fast
schwarzes Aussehen mit einer ein Pixel breiten Bronzelinie zurück. Das Aussehen folgt
dem Client und hat keinen Schalter. Klassenfarben und die Markierung des aktuellen
Charakters bleiben unverändert. Retail, Mists Classic, TBC Anniversary und Classic
Era sehen genau aus wie in 0.3.7. Spielzeit, gespeicherte Schlüssel, Schema 3 und
Companion-Protokoll 4 sind unverändert. Das ZIP bei geschlossenem WoW nach
`Interface/AddOns` entpacken.

Die automatischen Prüfungen stehen in der verlinkten Validierung, der Entwurf im
Theme-Dokument. Der Autor hat das neue Aussehen im Live-Client von Forever getestet.
Für Retail und die Classic-Clients vergleicht ein automatischer Test jede sichtbare
Fläche mit 0.3.7.

releases.name: Hourstone 0.3.7 – Azeroth Hours
releases.notes:
# Hourstone 0.3.7 — 2026-11-05

Hourstone 0.3.7 shows synchronized **WoW: Forever** characters as **WoW: Forever**
on every client. Until now, Hourstone labelled only the Forever characters that the
account's own database had recorded; those of another account or another PC appeared
under Retail everywhere, Forever included. **This needs Companion 0.2.2 or newer** on
the PC that runs WoW. It names the Forever installations, its own and those that other
PCs report, in the `Hourstone_Sync` data addon, and Hourstone labels the received
characters that come from them. With an older Companion, these characters stay under
Retail as before.

The client filter now offers WoW: Forever on every client whenever the list shows a
Forever character, and Retail's progress view treats these characters as
unsupported. For characters the account has recorded itself, its own label still
decides, so a `WTF` folder copied from Retail into Forever keeps its Retail entries.
A database copied into Forever counts as the client it was copied from wherever that
original is also synchronized.

**Forever surnames:** live Forever reports a character's surname where other clients
report the realm, so earlier versions showed "Magni" with the realm "Wildschuss" and
listed surnames in the realm filter. Hourstone 0.3.7 saves the full name, such as
"Magni Wildschuss", and the realm that WoW reports, such as "CAMWOW EU4 Realm 10 RP".
Each character is corrected at its next login in Forever.

The list is an optional addition to Companion protocol 4
([addendum](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/v0.3.7/docs/sync-protocol-v4-forever.md)).
Forever characters stay in the Retail client family; saved keys, playtime, merging,
SavedVariables schema 3 and protocol 4 are unchanged. Hourstone 0.3.2 to 0.3.6
ignore the list, so PCs can be updated one at a time. Nothing else changes for
Retail and Classic clients. With WoW closed, extract `Hourstone-0.3.7.zip` into
`Interface/AddOns`.

Automated checks are described in
[validation](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/v0.3.7/docs/VALIDATION.md).
The author tested 0.3.7 in the live clients with Companion 0.2.2: synchronized
Forever characters show as WoW: Forever, and a Forever character shows its full name
with the realm WoW reports after logging in. Retail's client filter and progress
view and the Classic clients were not separately tested in-game.

## Deutsch

Hourstone 0.3.7 zeigt synchronisierte Charaktere aus **WoW: Forever** auf jedem
Client als **WoW: Forever** an. Bisher hat Hourstone nur die Forever-Charaktere so
gekennzeichnet, die die eigene Datenbank des Accounts erfasst hat; die eines anderen
Accounts oder PCs standen überall unter Retail, auch in Forever. **Dafür ist Companion
ab 0.2.2** auf dem PC nötig, auf dem WoW läuft. Er nennt die Forever-Installationen,
die eigenen und die von anderen PCs gemeldeten, im Datenaddon `Hourstone_Sync`, und
Hourstone kennzeichnet die empfangenen Charaktere daraus. Mit einem älteren Companion
bleiben diese Charaktere wie bisher unter Retail.

Der Clientfilter bietet WoW: Forever jetzt auf jedem Client an, sobald die Liste einen
Forever-Charakter zeigt, und die Retail-Fortschrittsansicht behandelt diese
Charaktere als nicht unterstützt. Für selbst erfasste Charaktere entscheidet weiter
die Kennzeichnung des eigenen Accounts; ein von Retail nach Forever kopierter
`WTF`-Ordner behält daher seine Retail-Einträge. Eine nach Forever kopierte Datenbank
zählt als der Client, von dem sie stammt, sofern dieses Original ebenfalls abgeglichen
wird.

**Nachnamen in Forever:** Der Live-Client von Forever meldet den Nachnamen eines
Charakters dort, wo andere Clients den Realm melden. Frühere Versionen zeigten daher
„Magni“ mit dem Realm „Wildschuss“ und führten Nachnamen im Realmfilter. Hourstone
0.3.7 speichert den vollständigen Namen, etwa „Magni Wildschuss“, und den von WoW
gemeldeten Realm, etwa „CAMWOW EU4 Realm 10 RP“. Jeder Charakter wird bei seinem
nächsten Login in Forever korrigiert.

Die Liste ist eine optionale Ergänzung zu Companion-Protokoll 4. Forever-Charaktere
bleiben in der Clientfamilie Retail; Schlüssel, Spielzeit, Zusammenführung, Schema 3
und Protokoll 4 sind unverändert. Hourstone 0.3.2 bis 0.3.6 ignorieren die Liste,
die PCs können also einzeln aktualisiert werden. Sonst ändert sich für Retail- und
Classic-Clients nichts. Das ZIP bei geschlossenem WoW nach `Interface/AddOns`
entpacken. Die automatischen Prüfungen stehen in der verlinkten Validierung. Der Autor hat 0.3.7
mit Companion 0.2.2 in den Live-Clients getestet: Synchronisierte
Forever-Charaktere erscheinen als WoW: Forever, und ein Forever-Charakter zeigt nach
dem Login seinen vollständigen Namen mit dem von WoW gemeldeten Realm. Clientfilter
und Fortschrittsansicht in Retail sowie die Classic-Clients wurden nicht gesondert im
Spiel getestet.

releases.name: Hourstone 0.3.6 – Azeroth Hours
releases.notes:
# Hourstone 0.3.6 — 2026-11-05

Hourstone 0.3.6 shows **WoW: Forever** characters as **WoW: Forever** instead of
Retail. In the Forever client, the client column, the row tooltip and the client sort
use the new label, and the client filter offers WoW: Forever next to Retail. Forever
characters still belong to the Retail client family for saved keys, removal from the
overview and Companion protocol 4, which has no separate Forever family; Hourstone
stores the label as a separate marker beside it.

If Hourstone created its database in Forever after the launch on 4 November 2026 at
23:00 UTC, the characters that 0.3.5 or earlier recorded there change their label on
the first load of 0.3.6 in Forever; so do entries that an earlier version filed under
an unknown client such as `project-18`. In an older database, such as a `WTF` folder
copied from Retail, characters stay under Retail until they log in again in Forever.
From now on, every Hourstone database records the client that last loaded it, so a
database copied from another client running 0.3.6 or later is never relabelled.

**Synchronization:** a synchronized observation of a Forever character keeps the
label in Forever, and Retail's progress view treats Forever characters as
unsupported. Protocol 4 carries no client marker, so every client, Forever included,
still lists synchronized Forever characters that the account has not recorded itself,
such as another account's or another PC's, under Retail. Companion 0.2.1 and newer
already label them as WoW: Forever.

Nothing else changes for Retail and Classic clients. Saved characters, playtime and
settings are preserved; SavedVariables schema 3 and Companion protocol 4 are
unchanged, and the Companion ignores the new markers. With WoW closed, extract
`Hourstone-0.3.6.zip` into `Interface/AddOns`.

Automated checks are described in
[validation](https://github.com/krebs3r/hourstone-azeroth-hours/blob/v0.3.6/docs/VALIDATION.md).
The author tested this build in the live WoW: Forever client (build 1.60.1.70790):
characters recorded by 0.3.5 and by 0.3.6 show as WoW: Forever. The live client's
interface number has not been recorded yet, and Retail and Classic were not
separately tested in-game for this release.

## Deutsch

Hourstone 0.3.6 zeigt Charaktere aus **WoW: Forever** als **WoW: Forever** statt als
Retail an. Im Forever-Client verwenden Clientspalte, Zeilen-Tooltip und
Client-Sortierung die neue Bezeichnung, und der Clientfilter bietet WoW: Forever
neben Retail an. Für gespeicherte Schlüssel, das Löschen aus der Übersicht und
Companion-Protokoll 4, das keine eigene Forever-Familie kennt, bleiben
Forever-Charaktere in der Clientfamilie Retail; Hourstone speichert die Bezeichnung
als eigene Markierung daneben.

Hat Hourstone seine Datenbank nach dem Start am 5. November 2026 um 0:00 Uhr MEZ in
Forever angelegt, erhalten die Charaktere, die 0.3.5 oder älter dort erfasst hat, die
neue Bezeichnung beim ersten Laden von 0.3.6 in Forever; ebenso Einträge, die eine
frühere Version unter einem unbekannten Client wie `project-18` abgelegt hat. In einer
älteren Datenbank, etwa einem von Retail kopierten `WTF`-Ordner, bleiben Charaktere
unter Retail, bis sie sich erneut in Forever einloggen. Ab jetzt merkt sich jede
Hourstone-Datenbank, welcher Client sie zuletzt geladen hat; eine von einem anderen
Client mit 0.3.6 oder neuer kopierte Datenbank wird daher nie umbenannt.

**Abgleich:** Eine synchronisierte Beobachtung eines Forever-Charakters behält in
Forever die Bezeichnung, und die Retail-Fortschrittsansicht behandelt
Forever-Charaktere als nicht unterstützt. Weil Protokoll 4 keine Client-Markierung
überträgt, führt jeder Client, auch Forever, synchronisierte Forever-Charaktere, die
der Account nicht selbst erfasst hat, etwa die eines anderen Accounts oder PCs,
weiterhin unter Retail. Companion ab 0.2.1 zeigt sie bereits als WoW: Forever an.

Sonst ändert sich für Retail- und Classic-Clients nichts. Charaktere, Spielzeit und
Einstellungen bleiben erhalten; Schema 3 und Companion-Protokoll 4 sind unverändert,
und der Companion ignoriert die neuen Markierungen. Das ZIP bei geschlossenem WoW nach
`Interface/AddOns` entpacken. Die automatischen Prüfungen stehen in der verlinkten
Validierung. Der Autor hat diesen Build im Live-Client von WoW: Forever (Build
1.60.1.70790) getestet: Von 0.3.5 und von 0.3.6 erfasste Charaktere erscheinen als
WoW: Forever. Die Interface-Nummer des Live-Clients ist noch nicht erfasst, und
Retail und Classic wurden für diese Version nicht gesondert im Spiel getestet.
